prompt: Which of these is a setting that belongs in key-value storage?

choices.text: the access token the server issued
choices.why: A secret goes in the Keystore or the Keychain.

choices.text: the list of study sessions
choices.why: That grows with use; it belongs in the database.

choices.text: the day the week starts on
choices.why: Right. One name, one small value, read at launch.

choices.text: a course's cover picture, encoded as a string
choices.why: Large data goes in a file in the sandbox.

prompt: What do DataStore, UserDefaults, Async Storage and MMKV have in common, according to the lesson?

choices.text: The whole set lives in one file, read and rewritten whole
choices.why: Right, which is why they suit ten settings and not a thousand sessions.

choices.text: Each one is a small SQL database with a simpler interface
choices.why: None of them runs queries; they map names to values.

choices.text: They are asynchronous
choices.why: UserDefaults and MMKV answer synchronously; the table in the lesson says so.

choices.text: They encrypt what they store
choices.why: They write plain files in the sandbox, which is why secrets stay out.

prompt: Match each store to how a read reaches the app.

pairs.right: a Flow, off the main thread
synchronously, from a property list held in memory

prompt: `load` in kv.ts finds a file that does not parse. Why does it let the error through instead of returning {}?

choices.text: Because JSON.parse cannot be wrapped in try
choices.why: It can; the choice is deliberate.

choices.text: To make the app crash, which is the safest outcome
choices.why: The caller decides what to do; crashing is one possible choice, not the point.

choices.text: A missing file raises the same error, so they are handled together
choices.why: A missing file returns an empty store; the two are different answers.

choices.text: {} would reset the settings silently
choices.why: Right. A damaged file is something going wrong, and the caller should know.

prompt: A version of `save` writes the temporary file and renames it, but leaves out `fsyncSync`. What can a power cut leave behind?

choices.text: Two files called settings.json
choices.why: A folder holds one file per name.

choices.text: The new name on a file whose data never reached the disk
choices.why: Right. The rename can be written before the data it points at.

choices.text: The old settings, because a rename waits for the data anyway
choices.why: It does not wait; that is what fsync is there to force.

choices.text: A temporary file the next save will refuse to overwrite
choices.why: The next save opens it with "w" and writes over it.

prompt: After `node settings.ts set dailyGoal 45`, what does `node settings.ts get dailyGoal` print?

choices.text: "45", in quotes, as a string
choices.why: set turns anything numeric into a number.
Right. It is stored as the number 45.

choices.text: (no dailyGoal)
choices.why: The value was saved before it was read.

choices.text: saved 41 bytes
choices.why: That is what set prints, not get.

prompt: Why is the window in which a write can be torn larger than the time it takes to write the bytes you changed?

choices.text: Because the disk writes one setting at a time
choices.why: The disk knows nothing of settings; it writes bytes.

choices.text: Because JSON is slow to produce
choices.why: Speed is not the issue; the empty file is.

choices.text: Because the app writes the file twice, once to check it
choices.why: kv.ts writes it once.

choices.text: Opening with "w" empties the file before any byte is written
choices.why: Right. From that instant the only copy on disk is incomplete.

prompt: In the lesson's run, how many bytes of torn.json had been written when the in-place save stopped?
A team writes the temporary file to the phone's SD card and renames it into the app's internal storage. What has it lost?

choices.text: Atomicity: it becomes a copy and a delete
choices.why: Right. That is why the temporary file goes beside the real one.

choices.text: Nothing; a rename is the same step on any disk
choices.why: Across two disks it is not one.

choices.text: The backup, because the SD card is left out of it
choices.why: Possibly true, and not what breaks the save.

choices.text: The fsync, which does not work on SD cards
choices.why: fsync works there; the problem is the move between disks.

prompt: Renaming a file over another on the same disk is ___: a reader finds the old version or the new one, never half.
In grow.ts the file holds 95.6 KB after 1,000 sessions. Why did getting there write 46.70 MB?

choices.text: JSON stores numbers as text, which takes about five hundred times the space
choices.why: The file itself is 95.6 KB; the size of the encoding is not the cause.

choices.text: fsync doubles every write
choices.why: fsync pushes the same bytes to disk; it does not write them twice.

choices.text: Each save rewrote every earlier session
choices.why: Right. One tap's cost grows with the history.

choices.text: The temporary files were never deleted
choices.why: Each one was renamed over the real file.

prompt: Which of these go somewhere other than key-value storage? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a refresh token
choices.why: A secret: the Keystore or the Keychain.

choices.text: the notes the person wrote for each session
choices.why: They grow with use: the database.

choices.text: whether onboarding was shown
choices.why: One flag that never grows: a setting.

choices.text: the language the person picked
choices.why: One small value read at launch: a setting.

prompt: What is the lesson's test for whether something is a setting?

choices.text: Whether the key count grows with use
choices.why: Right. If it grows with use, it is not a setting.

choices.text: Whether the server also has a copy
choices.why: Where else it lives does not decide where it lives here.

choices.text: Whether it is read at launch
choices.why: A key-value store reads everything at launch; that is the cost, not the test.

choices.text: Whether it fits in under a kilobyte today
choices.why: Today's size says nothing about next year's.

prompt: A React Native planner stores each session's notes in MMKV under the key `notes:<session id>`, because MMKV is fast. A year later, what has gone wrong?

choices.text: MMKV reached its maximum of one thousand keys
choices.why: No such maximum is the problem; the shape of the data is.

choices.text: The notes were encrypted and the key was lost
choices.why: Nothing in the setup encrypts them.

choices.text: The keys grow with use, all held in memory
choices.why: Right. Being fast does not change what belongs there.

choices.text: Async Storage overwrote them
choices.why: The two stores keep separate files.

prompt: Put the steps of kv.ts's `save` in the order it does them.
After `node torn.ts rename` stops halfway, what does the next launch read?

choices.text: The new settings, completed from the temporary file
choices.why: Nothing reads the temporary file; it is half written.

choices.text: The old settings, whole
choices.why: Right. torn.json was never opened for writing.

choices.text: An empty store, because the file was emptied
choices.why: The file emptied was torn.json.tmp, not torn.json.

choices.text: A parse error at position 31
choices.why: That is the in-place run.

prompt: An Android app keeps its refresh token in DataStore, which writes atomically. Which problem from the lesson remains?

choices.text: The torn write, because DataStore writes in place
choices.why: DataStore writes a temporary file and renames it.

choices.text: The quadratic cost of grow.ts
choices.why: One token does not grow with use.

choices.text: The read blocks the main thread
choices.why: DataStore reads through a Flow, off the main thread.

choices.text: It is a plain file in the sandbox, in the backup
choices.why: Right. Atomic is not secret; the token belongs in the Keystore.

prompt: What does SwiftUI's `@AppStorage` read and write?

choices.text: A SwiftData model
choices.why: SwiftData is a database; @AppStorage is not part of it.

choices.text: The Keychain
choices.why: The Keychain holds secrets and has an API of its own.

choices.text: UserDefaults, through a property wrapper
choices.why: Right. It is the same store with a wrapper around it.

choices.text: A file in Library/Caches/
choices.why: A setting in the cache could be purged.
